title: Only now
hookLine: each lives only this moment; the rest is gone or unknown (Meditations 3.10)

cards: Where are you right now? Not your body. Your mind.
Maybe it's replaying a conversation from Tuesday, or rehearsing one for Friday.

The past rides along like a backpack, the future hangs ahead like a weather forecast, and the one place you actually stand gets barely a glance. Marcus Aurelius set all of that down in a few short lines. Today: only now.

teach.b: The tenth entry of book three opens with a clearing-out: throw everything else away, Marcus tells himself, and hold on to these few things.
Each of us, he says, lives only the present, this moment that can't be divided. Everything else is either already lived or uncertain. That's not a mood.
It's a description. You can't live yesterday again, and you can't yet live tomorrow. In his terms, the only life anyone actually has is happening in this breath.

teach.h: SHORT LIFE, SMALL CORNER, SHORT FAME.
teach.b: Short is the life each person lives. Small is the corner of the earth where they live it.
Short, too, is the longest fame after death, passed along by people who will soon die themselves, who don't know even themselves, let alone someone long gone. He isn't trying to depress himself.

He's pulling his attention back from where it wanders, the regrets and the legacy, to the one place it can do any good. If the past is finished and the future unknown, neither is where your choices happen.

teach.h: THE ONLY PART YOU CAN STEER.
teach.b: The present is small, but it's the only part of life you can steer. Other contemplative traditions have their own words for returning to this moment. For Marcus, it's plain arithmetic.
As he put it back in book two, the present is the only thing anyone can lose, because it's the only thing anyone has.

how: Some readers of Marcus Aurelius return to Meditations 3.10 when worry or regret pulls at them, bringing their attention back to the present moment.

o: each of us lives only this moment; the rest is lived or unknown
plans for the future are pointless, so never make any
forget your past entirely so it can never hurt you again

p: short, and passed on by the dying

s: Marcus says each person lives only the present moment
everything else, he says, is either already lived or uncertain.
Marcus promises lasting fame to those who live well
he says even the longest fame is short.
Marcus says the present is too small to matter
he calls it a point that can't be divided, and the only time anyone lives.

games.q: you're at dinner with a friend, and your mind is replaying a meeting from this morning. what fits 3.10?
o: keep replaying it until it's solved.
notice it's already lived, and come back to the table.
games.why: Marcus says the past is already lived; the present, here at the table, is the only life you have.

practice: Feel this breath, the cool air coming in, the slight warmth going out: that's the whole of your life right now. When your mind drifts to earlier, say quietly, gone; when it drifts to later, say, unknown.
Then come back to this breath, and this one.

wordCard.voice: Only now. Marcus says each person lives only this moment; the past is already lived, and the future is uncertain. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek, 'the present': the moment Marcus says is all each of us lives.

carryVoice: Your line: only this. The past already lived, the future uncertain. Day five hundred forty-five, done.
